description: Issue #839 AC2, the cross-kind collision in the STRUCT-FIRST direction: `struct tally [ x y ]` then `define tally`. Its mirror (`define` then `struct`) is `struct-reserved-word-procedure`. Having both directions is what makes the pair meaningful: an implementation that only checked a `struct` name against already-declared procedures — but not a `define` name against already-declared structs — would report the mirror and be silent here, so this fixture is the one that fails for it. `spec/error-model.md:126` covers exactly this case: "a procedure and a struct with the same name in either order". Note what neither direction can show: whether the runtime keeps one first-declaration map or two with a cross-kind lookup — those are indistinguishable from source, so no description here claims it.
